about: The quote-matching rule of plans/relations-followups.md §2.2, as cases both matchers must pass: Python's locate_quote (scripts/derivations_reference.py --selftest-units) and Swift's CurationQuote.contains (CurationQuoteTests). The rule: turn CRLF and a lone CR into LF, and split lines at LF only; normalise page and quote to NFC; collapse every run of space, tab and LF to one space, in both; then the quote must be a case-sensitive substring of the section, compared as Unicode scalars, never as grapheme clusters. A quote that collapses to nothing or to one space is never found. The section is the body under the first ATX heading whose text equals `section` (null: the whole file, frontmatter included): the lines after the heading line, up to the next heading of the same or a higher level (as many # or fewer), or the end of the file. A heading is a line that starts with 1 to 6 # and then a space; its text is the rest, trimmed of spaces and tabs, without a closing run of # that follows a space or tab. Lines in the frontmatter (a first line '---' up to the next line '---', trailing spaces and tabs ignored) and in fenced code blocks are not headings. A fence opens on a line of at most 3 spaces then 3 or more backticks or tildes, and closes on a line of at most 3 spaces, at least as many of the same character and nothing else but spaces and tabs, or at the end of the file. `line` is what Python reports: the 1-based line where the first match starts, counting lines after line breaks became LF. Swift answers found or not found only.
